## Natural history notes

A small darkling beetle characterized by an elongated dark brown to black body, hardened wing covers, and a slightly rough or pitted surface texture. In Florida, Glyptotus cribratus is associated with dead and decaying hardwood, with records from southern Florida in dry, soft, rotten live oak branches in maritime forest habitat. Adults and larvae live in rotten wood, where they help break down dead branches and recycle nutrients while also serving as prey for woodpeckers, lizards, spiders, predatory beetles, and parasitoid wasps.
